title: Review: convergence check round 5
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — Two structural API issues (error discrimination, sign/verify byte mismatch) will generate issue reports once callers build on top of this. The pathLen off-by-one is a security bypass that is unlikely to be hit in practice (requires a chain with two intermediates where the first has pathLen=0) but would be embarrassing if discovered. No credentials are logged, no unsafe code, no network calls.
Confidence: 85% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: MIME-6uo.3 (sign() CRLF issue) — the RFC 5751 transport encoding rules around CRLF canonicalization are complex and I may have the exact byte-for-byte comparison wrong; the OpenSSL test passing is evidence either way. MIME-6uo.2 (pathLen off-by-one) — RFC 5280 §4.2.1.9 language is dense and I am moderately confident the check should be >= not >, but the exact semantics of 'certs below' vs 'certs between' require careful re-reading. Uncertainty driven by: not reading the RFC text files directly from standards/, relying on memory of RFC 5280. Would raise confidence if: writing a unit test with a two-intermediate chain where first CA has pathLen=0 and verifying the current behavior.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — code is idiomatic Rust, uses ? correctly throughout, no gratuitous clones, no unwrap in non-test code, error types are structured. The primary non-idiomatic patterns are error variant misuse (Other where SignatureVerification applies) and the duplicated base64 folding. No lifetime issues, no Arc/Rc, no bool parameters.
